title: A flat change of coefficients is exact
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that for every
scheme $X$ the extension of scalars $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ along the coefficient change
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]) preserves finite limits. Then each
$\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ preserves homology (of complexes of $\Lambda_X$-modules).

proof.text: Fix a scheme $X$ and put $R=\Lambda_X$, $S=\Lambda'_X$, and $F=\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$, with $a_X$ as in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. These are internal modules in the tensor category of abelian sheaves, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. They are precisely the sheaves of modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], a map $R\otimes M\to M$ is a map from the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, and the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies this with a compatible family of bilinear maps $R(U)\times M(U)\to M(U)$. The unit and associativity equations are exactly the sectionwise module laws. The morphism equation $f\circ\gamma_M=\gamma_N\circ(R\otimes f)$ becomes $f_U(rm)=r f_U(m)$ on every object $U$, so the morphisms are precisely the sectionwise linear sheaf maps. For the ring objects, multiplication gives compatible bilinear products on $R(U)$ and $S(U)$, and the unit is the image of $1$ from the constant presheaf $\mathbf Z$ through the sheafified monoidal unit; the monoid equations give the sectionwise ring laws. Thus $R$ and $S$ are sheaves of rings. Thus the two module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in the coefficient universe in which the small pro-étale site is essentially small; that node's size hypothesis is satisfied. This identification changes neither the objects nor the morphisms or their compositions.

source.place: implicit abelian-category hypotheses in the final clause; module-object convention spelled out using the sheaf tensor definition

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], $F$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$. Its extension hypotheses hold here: the sheaf tensor is symmetric and closed and preserves colimits in each variable by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], the ambient category of abelian sheaves is abelian (apply [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] to the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf Z$), so it has coequalizers, and $R$ is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to each finite diagram in the source module category. Such diagrams are small, and the module categories are abelian, so the required finite colimits exist. It follows that $F$ preserves finite colimits, including the empty colimit and cokernels. The hypothesis of the item supplies preservation of finite limits, including kernels.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact, part (1); applied to the adjunction in the blueprint proof

proof.text: The preceding properties make $F$ additive. Indeed $F(0)$ is zero, since the zero object is both the empty limit and the empty colimit, so $F$ preserves zero morphisms by factoring them through zero. Under the finite product and coproduct identifications, $F$ sends the canonical biproduct injections and projections to the corresponding injections and projections: their component matrices have only identity and zero entries. Consequently it sends the diagonal $\Delta$, codiagonal $\nabla$ and block diagonal maps to their counterparts. Apply $F$ to $f+g=\nabla\circ\operatorname{diag}(f,g)\circ\Delta$ to obtain $F(f+g)=F(f)+F(g)$. Thus $F$ is an exact additive functor between the abelian categories of step 1.

source.place: Tag 0DLP, lemma-additive-functor, diagonal/codiagonal argument; Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, part (1)

proof.text: For any complex $K$ of $R$-modules and any degree $n$, take its three consecutive terms $K^{n-1}\xrightarrow{d^{n-1}}K^n\xrightarrow{d^n}K^{n+1}$. Their composite is zero; preservation of zero morphisms ensures the same for the image under $F$. Apply clause (c) of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to this three-term complex and the exact additive functor verified above. It gives $\ker F(d^n)/\operatorname{im}F(d^{n-1})\cong F(\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1})$, naturally in $K$. These are precisely $H^n(FK)$ and $F(H^nK)$. This works in every degree, without any bound on $K$, and for every chosen scheme $X$, proving the assertion.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, kernel/cokernel preservation applied to homology, as in the final clause of the blueprint proof
